title: How does disorder enter a model, a Hall current and a pump?
intro: Questions, solutions and this checklist form one set. Work down the main line. Tick a blue tool when you can calculate with it, an orange idea when you can reason with it, and a research link when a result closes it.

cumulants.name: Covariances and cumulants
cumulants.note: Describe a random variable beyond its variance, and two variables by their covariance.
cumulants.ref: N. G. van Kampen, Stochastic Processes in Physics and Chemistry (3rd ed., 2007), Ch. I

golden-rule.name: Fermi's golden rule
golden-rule.note: Turn a weak perturbation and a density of final states into a transition rate.
golden-rule.ref: J. J. Sakurai, J. Napolitano, Modern Quantum Mechanics (3rd ed., Cambridge, 2020), Ch. 5

disorder-average.name: Averaging matrix elements over disorder
disorder-average.note: Average products of random matrix elements in a plane-wave basis; only coinciding sites survive.
disorder-average.ref: P. A. Lee, T. V. Ramakrishnan, Disordered electronic systems, Rev. Mod. Phys. 57, 287 (1985)

gaussian-integrals.name: Gaussian integrals and small-angle expansions
gaussian-integrals.note: Evaluate integrals of e^(−αx²/2) and x² e^(−αx²/2), and expand a periodic integrand near its peak.

noise-spectrum.name: Noise spectra and transition rates
noise-spectrum.note: Fourier transform a correlation function and read the rate from the spectrum at the transition frequency.
noise-spectrum.ref: A. A. Clerk et al., Introduction to quantum noise, measurement, and amplification, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 1155 (2010), Sec. II

averages-of-functions.name: Averages of a function of a random variable
averages-of-functions.note: Estimate the mean shift and the spread of F(x) to leading order in the variance of x.
averages-of-functions.ref: Taylor expansions for the moments of functions of random variables (reference page)

berry-curvature.name: Berry curvature of a two-band Hamiltonian
berry-curvature.note: Compute Ω from the vector d(k) of H = ε₀ + d·σ, and integrate it over occupied states.
berry-curvature.ref: D. Xiao, M.-C. Chang, Q. Niu, Berry phase effects on electronic properties, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 1959 (2010), Sec. II

wavepacket-boltzmann.name: Wave-packet dynamics and the relaxation-time Boltzmann equation
wavepacket-boltzmann.note: Use ħk̇ = −eE, the anomalous velocity and f − f₀ = (eτ/ħ)E·∂f to build currents order by order.
wavepacket-boltzmann.ref: N. W. Ashcroft, N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics (1976), Chs. 12–13; Xiao, Chang, Niu (2010), Sec. III

fermi-surface-integrals.name: Integrals over the Fermi sea and Fermi surface
fermi-surface-integrals.note: Expand f₀ in a small parameter, turn ∂f₀ into a delta function on the Fermi circle and integrate in polar coordinates.
fermi-surface-integrals.ref: Dirac delta function: composition with a function (reference page)

complex-amplitudes.name: Complex amplitudes at second order
complex-amplitudes.note: Multiply two oscillating quantities and separate the 2ω and zero-frequency parts.
complex-amplitudes.ref: R. W. Boyd, Nonlinear Optics (3rd ed., Academic Press, 2008), Ch. 1

second-quantization.name: Fermion creation and annihilation operators
second-quantization.note: Read c†, c and n = c†c, and commute hopping terms with densities.
second-quantization.ref: A. Altland, B. Simons, Condensed Matter Field Theory (2nd ed., Cambridge, 2010), Ch. 2

products-of-random-numbers.name: Products of random numbers
products-of-random-numbers.note: Take logarithms: a long product of random factors grows or decays with the mean of the logarithm.

pauli-decomposition.name: Pauli decomposition of a 2×2 matrix
pauli-decomposition.note: Write a Hermitian 2×2 matrix as h₀ + h·σ and read bias and mixing from its entries.
pauli-decomposition.ref: M. A. Nielsen, I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (Cambridge, 2010), Sec. 2.1

gaussian-tails.name: Gaussian sums and tail probabilities
gaussian-tails.note: Add independent Gaussian variables and read tail probabilities from Φ(z).

poisson-events.name: Independent rare events
poisson-events.note: Probability of the first event among many independent sources; rates of independent sources add.

disorder-model.name: A disorder model: H for each configuration and its probability
disorder-model.note: Compute in one configuration first, then average; the averaged Hamiltonian is not enough.
disorder-model.ref: P. W. Anderson, Absence of diffusion in certain random lattices, Phys. Rev. 109, 1492 (1958)

projection-to-orbitals.name: From a defect potential to lattice parameters
projection-to-orbitals.note: Matrix elements of the defect potential between localized orbitals give on-site and bond terms together.
projection-to-orbitals.ref: N. W. Ashcroft, N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics (1976), Ch. 10 (tight-binding method)

correlated-disorder.name: Correlated disorder from one microscopic source
correlated-disorder.note: Sample positions or impurities, then compute every parameter from them; channels and neighbours are correlated.
correlated-disorder.ref: A. Browaeys, T. Lahaye, Many-body physics with individually controlled Rydberg atoms, Nat. Phys. 16, 132 (2020)

quantum-vs-transport-lifetime.name: Quantum lifetime versus transport lifetime
quantum-vs-transport-lifetime.note: A level width and a current relaxation time weight scattering angles differently.
quantum-vs-transport-lifetime.ref: S. Das Sarma, F. Stern, Single-particle relaxation time versus scattering time in an impure electron gas, Phys. Rev. B 32, 8442 (1985)

localization.name: Localization, mean free path and dephasing
localization.note: Interference localizes waves after a few mean free paths in one dimension unless phase memory is lost first.
localization.ref: B. Kramer, A. MacKinnon, Localization: theory and experiment, Rep. Prog. Phys. 56, 1469 (1993)

rate-validity.name: When does a decay rate exist?
rate-validity.note: A static Hamiltonian gives oscillations; a rate needs many final levels within the width and times below the Heisenberg time.
rate-validity.ref: J. J. Sakurai, J. Napolitano, Modern Quantum Mechanics (3rd ed., Cambridge, 2020), Ch. 5

static-vs-dynamic.name: Static versus fluctuating disorder
static-vs-dynamic.note: Spectral weight at the transition frequency and the observation time decide; static terms belong in H.
static-vs-dynamic.ref: A. A. Clerk et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 1155 (2010)

self-averaging.name: Mean shift versus self-averaging spread
self-averaging.note: A bias of every region survives the sample average; region-to-region spread falls as 1/√N.
self-averaging.ref: J. Martin et al., Observation of electron–hole puddles in graphene, Nat. Phys. 4, 144 (2008)

ahe-mechanisms.name: Intrinsic, side-jump and skew-scattering Hall currents
ahe-mechanisms.note: Three microscopic sources of a Hall current and how they scale with the impurity density.
ahe-mechanisms.ref: N. Nagaosa, J. Sinova, S. Onoda, A. H. MacDonald, N. P. Ong, Anomalous Hall effect, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 1539 (2010)

time-reversal-geometry.name: Time reversal and the Berry curvature
time-reversal-geometry.note: Ω is odd under time reversal: linear Hall currents cancel between partners, curvature dipoles add.
time-reversal-geometry.ref: D. Xiao, M.-C. Chang, Q. Niu, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 1959 (2010)

power-counting.name: Counting powers of τ
power-counting.note: Each impurity factor is 1/τ, each order in E brings τ: compare mechanisms by their disorder dependence.
power-counting.ref: N. A. Sinitsyn, Semiclassical theories of the anomalous Hall effect, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 20, 023201 (2008)

curvature-dipole.name: The Berry curvature dipole
curvature-dipole.note: A second-order Hall current from the first moment of Ω over the Fermi sea; needs broken inversion.
curvature-dipole.ref: I. Sodemann, L. Fu, Quantum nonlinear Hall effect induced by Berry curvature dipole, Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 216806 (2015)

frequency-regimes.name: Low versus high frequency (ωτ)
frequency-regimes.note: At ωτ ≫ 1 a relaxation-time response stops depending on τ; scaling tests change meaning.
frequency-regimes.ref: I. Sodemann, L. Fu, Phys. Rev. Lett. 115, 216806 (2015)

disorder-nlhe.name: Disorder-induced nonlinear Hall currents
disorder-nlhe.note: Side jump and skew scattering at second order, computed for a tilted Dirac cone.
disorder-nlhe.ref: Z. Z. Du, C. M. Wang, S. Li, H.-Z. Lu, X. C. Xie, Nat. Commun. 10, 3047 (2019)

theory-level.name: The level of theory can change a sign
theory-level.note: A diagrammatic calculation keeps the scaling but reverses the collision terms of the Boltzmann result.
theory-level.ref: Z. Z. Du, C. M. Wang, H.-P. Sun, H.-Z. Lu, X. C. Xie, Nat. Commun. 12, 5038 (2021)

scaling-law.name: Scaling with the longitudinal conductivity
scaling-law.note: Plot E_y/E_x² against σ to separate mechanisms by their powers of τ; several sources mix.
scaling-law.ref: Z. Z. Du et al., Nat. Commun. 10, 3047 (2019)

moments-not-width.name: One broadening, different disorder
moments-not-width.note: Γ fixes the second moment only; the sign of the third moment changes a response.
moments-not-width.ref: N. Nagaosa et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 1539 (2010), Sec. IV

average-symmetry.name: Symmetry on average
average-symmetry.note: An ensemble can be symmetric when no sample is; averaged quantities obey the symmetry.
average-symmetry.ref: R. Ma, C. Wang, Average symmetry-protected topological phases, Phys. Rev. X 13, 031016 (2023)

statistical-degeneracy.name: Statistically degenerate edges
statistical-degeneracy.note: Two edges differ in every sample but have the same distribution over the ensemble.
statistical-degeneracy.ref: Z. Yue et al., Average topological phase in a disordered Rydberg atom array, arXiv:2505.06286

chiral-chain.name: Edge states of a dimer chain
chiral-chain.note: Zero-energy edge states of a two-site-per-cell chain and when they exist.
chiral-chain.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (2016), Ch. 1

topology-from-disorder.name: Topology from disorder
topology-from-disorder.note: The logarithmic mean of the hoppings decides the phase of a random chiral chain.
topology-from-disorder.ref: I. Mondragon-Shem, T. L. Hughes, J. Song, E. Prodan, Phys. Rev. Lett. 113, 046802 (2014)

thouless-pump.name: Adiabatic (Thouless) pumping
thouless-pump.note: A slow periodic change of a lattice carries an integer number of particles per period.
thouless-pump.ref: D. J. Thouless, Quantization of particle transport, Phys. Rev. B 27, 6083 (1983)

local-charge-bookkeeping.name: Counting charge with bond currents
local-charge-bookkeeping.note: Continuity on a lattice: differences of bond charges count accumulation in a region.
local-charge-bookkeeping.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (2016), Ch. 4

twist-chern.name: A Chern number without momentum
twist-chern.note: Replace k by a flux through the ring and average the pumped charge over it.
twist-chern.ref: Q. Niu, D. J. Thouless, J. Phys. A 17, 2453 (1984); Q. Niu, D. J. Thouless, Y.-S. Wu, Phys. Rev. B 31, 3372 (1985)

fractional-pump.name: Two-cycle fractional pumping
fractional-pump.note: Particles follow one of two localized orbitals per cell that exchange every period.
fractional-pump.ref: M. Jürgensen, J. Steiner, G. Refael, M. C. Rechtsman, Multi-band fractional Thouless pumps, arXiv:2504.09338

bias-vs-mixing.name: A random potential as a bias or a mixing
bias-vs-mixing.note: Projected onto two orbitals, the same potential acts along z or x depending on the orbital shapes.
bias-vs-mixing.ref: M. Jürgensen et al., arXiv:2504.09338 (flavor orbitals)

periodic-sign-reversal.name: A static potential seen by a moving orbital
periodic-sign-reversal.note: When the followed orbital exchanges flavor each period, a static bias reverses its sign.

domain-energetics.name: Domains and domain walls
domain-energetics.note: A reversed block costs wall energy and gains bulk energy; energy alone is not a rate.
domain-energetics.ref: M. Jürgensen et al., arXiv:2504.09338 (domain excitations)

imry-ma.name: The random-field (Imry–Ma) argument
imry-ma.note: Random energy grows as √ℓ, a wall costs a fixed amount: some block always wins in a long chain.
imry-ma.ref: Y. Imry, S.-k. Ma, Random-field instability of the ordered state of continuous symmetry, Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 1399 (1975)

rare-regions.name: Rare regions
rare-regions.note: Atypical local disorder dominates when the system is large enough to contain it.
rare-regions.ref: T. Vojta, Rare region effects at classical, quantum and nonequilibrium phase transitions, J. Phys. A 39, R143 (2006)

lifetime-definitions.name: First event versus macroscopic failure
lifetime-definitions.note: The first defect comes earlier in a larger system; the transport lifetime need not.
lifetime-definitions.ref: D. Abanin, W. De Roeck, W. W. Ho, F. Huveneers, Commun. Math. Phys. 354, 809 (2017)

real-sample-model.name: Disorder model of a real sample
real-sample-model.note: Defect potentials projected on Wannier orbitals and defect statistics give κₙ and K(q).

collision-coefficients.name: τ¹ collision coefficients for that disorder
collision-coefficients.note: Diagrammatic Kubo theory (non-crossing) for the real bands and defect T-matrices.

finite-frequency-collisions.name: Collision terms at finite frequency
finite-frequency-collisions.note: Side jump and skew scattering as functions of ωτ.

dressed-flavor-fields.name: Random fields of the correlated flavors
dressed-flavor-fields.note: Project on-site and bond disorder onto the dressed many-body flavors over the whole cycle.

semiclassics-consistent.name: A consistent semiclassical theory at second order
semiclassics-consistent.note: Boltzmann side jump misses terms found diagrammatically; near the band edge ħ/(ε_Fτ) is not small.

rare-region-nucleation.name: Nucleation of domains in rare regions
rare-region-nucleation.note: Prethermalization theorems need a fast drive or a uniform gap; here the drive is slow and gaps close locally.

wall-motion.name: Domain-wall motion in an alternating random field
wall-motion.note: Equilibrium creep theory assumes thermal activation; these walls are quantum and driven.

two-state-chern.name: Chern number of a two-state manifold without a uniform gap
two-state-chern.note: The Niu–Thouless argument needs a gap uniform in N, which rare regions remove.
two-state-chern.ref: Niu, Thouless, Wu, Phys. Rev. B 31, 3372 (1985)

average-spt-transport.name: Transport protected by an average symmetry
average-spt-transport.note: Classifications concern ensembles of states, not their driven response.
average-spt-transport.ref: L. Hertkorn, Y. Oreg, Topology from disorder, Nat. Phys. 22, 1534 (2026)

start.title: Start: the four core physics courses
start.text: Reader: an undergraduate who knows classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics and statistical physics. Each question lists only what it needs beyond that.

end.title: Research target
end.text: Predict, for a specified disorder, how large the second-order Hall response is and how long a fractional pump keeps its transport in a large system.

groups.title: From a dirty crystal to a random Hamiltonian
groups.note: Which random terms must a model of a real material contain first, and how do they become the scattering rate and the broadening of response theories?

footer: An item appears in full where it is first needed and as a dashed reminder later. Ticks stay in this browser.

Shared gap of the O-theory links: the useful quantity is a rare-region rate or an ensemble-symmetry constraint, not an averaged energy or a single broadening, and no gap or small parameter is uniform in the system size.
